about: Reference Knowledge map of the gold course, written by Claude Opus 5.5 in one pass over material.pdf (55 pages, uploaded to staging as Linear_Algebra_I_Script_WS2026-27), with the extraction prompt's KC rule: one thing an exam task could test on its own and a Student could learn in one sitting. It is the bar a pipeline run is judged against (coverage, granularity, Prerequisites, Topics, Exercises and answer keys). Pages are PDF pages. Written 2026-11-07 for PR #252.
granularity: 107 KCs taught by the lecture notes (pp. 10-38, 29 pages: about 37 per 10 pages) and 6 KCs taught only by the Exercises and old exams. A judge counts a pipeline KC as matching when it is the same, or one step finer or coarser.

notKcs.what: Title page and 'About this script'; the cover figure (parallelogram) illustrates Remark 6.4.6 and is no KC by itself
Course information: welcome, organisation, admission, exam format and dates, grading, schedule, literature, advice (admin)
Notation and conventions; its one exam-relevant fact is that statements marked (*) are not relevant for the exam
Remark 3.3.4 (cost of elimination vs. Leibniz) is a side remark, not a KC
Section 7.5 Outlook: Linear Algebra II material (triangularisation, Cayley-Hamilton in general, Jordan form, spectral theorem)
Exercise collection intro and 'How to write up a proof' (admin)

assumedFromOutside: Integer divisibility, primes and division with remainder (Z/nZ, Theorem 2.2.4)
Polynomials: degree, roots, polynomial division (fundamental theorem of algebra, characteristic polynomial)
Analysis I: continuity, derivatives, integrals; sin, cos, exp (function spaces, Ex. 9, Resit P4)
Countability of Q and R (dim_Q R is infinite)
Axiom of choice and Zorn's lemma (right inverses, Remark 4.3.9*)
Plane geometry: area, volume, rotation by an angle (Examples 5.1.2, 7.2.3, Remark 6.4.6)
Proof of the fundamental theorem of algebra (Complex Analysis)

topics.name: Logic and proof
topics.centralQuestion: How are statements combined, negated and proved?

topics.name: Sets and maps
topics.centralQuestion: When is a map injective, surjective or invertible?

topics.name: Relations and induction
topics.centralQuestion: How do equivalence relations partition a set, and how does induction prove statements for all n?

topics.name: Groups
topics.centralQuestion: What is a group, and what do homomorphisms and their kernels tell us?

topics.name: Rings, fields and complex numbers
topics.centralQuestion: Which number systems are fields, and how do we compute in F_p and C?

topics.name: Linear systems and Gaussian elimination
topics.centralQuestion: How do we decide whether Ax = b is solvable and describe all its solutions?

topics.name: Vector spaces and subspaces
topics.centralQuestion: What is a vector space, and which subsets are subspaces?

topics.name: Independence, bases and dimension
topics.centralQuestion: What is a basis, and why do all bases have the same size?

topics.name: Sums of subspaces and computing in K^n
topics.centralQuestion: How do subspaces combine, and how do we compute bases, sums and intersections in K^n?

topics.name: Linear maps and rank-nullity
topics.centralQuestion: How do kernel and image of a linear map relate to the dimension of its domain?

topics.name: Matrices of linear maps, change of basis and rank
topics.centralQuestion: How does a matrix describe a linear map, and how does it change with the bases?

topics.name: Quotient spaces, elementary matrices and the dual space
topics.centralQuestion: How do quotients, elementary matrices and linear forms extend the theory of linear maps?

topics.name: Permutations and the determinant
topics.centralQuestion: What is the determinant, and how do we compute it?

topics.name: Laplace expansion, adjugate and Cramer's rule
topics.centralQuestion: How do minors give the determinant, the inverse and the solution of Ax = b?

topics.name: Eigenvalues and the characteristic polynomial
topics.centralQuestion: How do we find the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a matrix?

topics.name: Diagonalisation and its applications
topics.centralQuestion: When is a matrix diagonalisable, and what does diagonalising it buy us?

kcs.name: Logical connectives and truth tables
kcs.description: Negation, and, or, implication, equivalence; an implication is false only when A is true and B false (ex falso quodlibet).

kcs.name: Tautologies: contraposition and De Morgan
kcs.description: (A => B) <=> (not B => not A); De Morgan's laws; an equivalence is two implications (Lemma 1.1.1).

kcs.name: Quantifiers and their negation
kcs.description: For all / there exists / exists exactly one; negation swaps the quantifiers; their order matters.

kcs.name: Proof techniques
kcs.description: Direct proof, contraposition, contradiction, proving equivalences and a cycle of implications; sqrt(2) is irrational (Remark 1.1.2, Example 1.1.3).

kcs.name: Sets and set operations
kcs.description: Elements, equality of sets, union, intersection, difference, disjoint sets, power set, families, Cartesian products and tuples.

kcs.name: Double inclusion
kcs.description: Prove A = B by showing A subset B and B subset A.

kcs.name: Maps, image and preimage
kcs.description: Domain, codomain, equality of maps, image f(A) and preimage f^-1(B), Map(X, Y).

kcs.name: Injective, surjective, bijective
kcs.description: Definitions (Definition 1.3.2) and how to prove or refute each property.

kcs.name: Composition and identity
kcs.description: g o f, associativity of composition, the identity map.

kcs.name: Left and right inverses and the inverse map
kcs.description: Injective iff left inverse, surjective iff right inverse, bijective iff two-sided inverse, which is unique (Proposition 1.3.3).

kcs.name: Maps between finite sets of equal size
kcs.description: For |X| = |Y| finite, injective <=> surjective <=> bijective (Corollary 1.3.4).

kcs.name: Equivalence relations and quotient sets
kcs.description: Reflexive, symmetric, transitive; equivalence classes; M/~ is a partition (Proposition 1.4.2).

kcs.name: Congruence modulo n and Z/nZ as a set
kcs.description: a = b mod n is an equivalence relation with n classes [0], ..., [n-1].

kcs.name: Proof by induction
kcs.description: Base case and induction step, strong induction; e.g. the sum 0 + ... + n.

kcs.name: Groups: axioms and examples
kcs.description: Associativity, neutral element, inverses, abelian groups; examples and non-examples, S(X) and S_n, invertible matrices.

kcs.name: Rules in a group
kcs.description: Uniqueness of neutral element and inverses, (ab)^-1 = b^-1 a^-1, cancellation, unique solution of ax = b (Lemma 2.1.2).

kcs.name: Subgroups
kcs.description: Definition 2.1.4 and checking it.

kcs.name: Group homomorphisms and kernel
kcs.description: phi(ab) = phi(a)phi(b); phi(e) = e', kernel is a subgroup, injective iff trivial kernel (Lemma 2.1.5).

kcs.name: Rings and fields
kcs.description: Ring and field axioms, 0a = 0, no zero divisors in a field; Q, R, C, Z, K[x], 2x2 matrices with zero divisors.

kcs.name: The ring Z/nZ
kcs.description: Addition and multiplication of classes are well defined; Z/nZ is a commutative ring with n elements.

kcs.name: Z/nZ is a field iff n is prime; computing in F_p
kcs.description: Theorem 2.2.4 and its proof via Corollary 1.3.4; inverses in F_p such as 2^-1 = 3 in F_5.

kcs.name: Characteristic of a field
kcs.description: char K is 0 or a prime; in characteristic 2, 1 + 1 = 0 and one cannot divide by 2.

kcs.name: Complex numbers
kcs.description: C as a field on R^2, a + bi, real and imaginary part, conjugate, modulus, inverse.

kcs.name: Fundamental theorem of algebra
kcs.description: Every non-constant complex polynomial has a root and splits into linear factors.
assumes: Proof of the fundamental theorem of algebra (Complex Analysis)

kcs.name: Matrices and linear systems
kcs.description: K^{m x n}, the product Ax, a system Ax = b, homogeneous systems, solution set L(A, b), augmented matrix.

kcs.name: Structure of the solution set
kcs.description: x -> Ax is additive and homogeneous; L(A, b) = x0 + L(A, 0) (Lemma 3.1.2).

kcs.name: Elementary row operations
kcs.description: (R1)-(R3) and why they do not change the solution set (Lemma 3.2.2).

kcs.name: Row echelon and reduced row echelon form
kcs.description: Pivots, pivot columns, zero rows (Definition 3.2.3).

kcs.name: Gaussian elimination
kcs.description: Bringing any matrix to reduced row echelon form by row operations (Theorem 3.2.4).

kcs.name: Reading off the solution
kcs.description: Solvability condition, pivot and free variables, general solution, uniqueness iff r = n (Theorem 3.3.1, Example 3.3.2).

kcs.name: More unknowns than equations
kcs.description: A homogeneous system with m < n has a non-zero solution (Theorem 3.3.1(c)).

kcs.name: Linear systems over finite fields
kcs.description: Elimination over F_p; a solvable system with n - r free variables has p^(n-r) solutions (Remark 3.3.3).

kcs.name: Vector spaces: axioms and examples
kcs.description: Definition 4.1.1; K^n, K^{m x n}, K^X, K[x], K[x]_<=d, field extensions, function spaces, the zero space.

kcs.name: Calculation rules in vector spaces
kcs.description: 0v = 0, lambda 0 = 0, (-1)v = -v, lambda v = 0 implies lambda = 0 or v = 0 (Lemma 4.1.2).

kcs.name: Subspaces
kcs.description: Criterion (U1)-(U3), examples and non-examples, L(A, 0) is a subspace and L(A, b) with b != 0 is not.

kcs.name: Intersections and unions of subspaces
kcs.description: Intersections are subspaces; U1 u U2 is one iff one contains the other (Lemma 4.2.3).

kcs.name: Linear combinations and span
kcs.description: span(S) as the set of linear combinations and the smallest subspace containing S; generating families.

kcs.name: Linear independence
kcs.description: Definition 4.3.1, families versus sets, a family with 0 or a repeated vector is dependent.

kcs.name: Dependence lemma
kcs.description: Dependent iff some vector lies in the span of the others (Lemma 4.3.3).

kcs.name: Testing independence in K^m
kcs.description: v1, ..., vn independent iff Ax = 0 has only the trivial solution for A = (v1|...|vn); more than m vectors in K^m are dependent (Example 4.3.4).

kcs.name: Bases and standard bases
kcs.description: A basis is an independent generating family; standard bases of K^n, K[x], K[x]_<=d, C over R, K^{m x n}.

kcs.name: Characterisation of bases and coordinates
kcs.description: Basis <=> minimal generating <=> maximal independent <=> unique representation; coordinates depend on the order (Theorem 4.3.7).

kcs.name: A finite generating family contains a basis
kcs.description: Every finitely generated space has a finite basis (Corollary 4.3.8).

kcs.name: Steinitz exchange lemma
kcs.description: An independent family is no longer than a generating family and can be exchanged into it (Theorem 4.4.1).

kcs.name: Dimension
kcs.description: All bases have the same size; dim V; dim K^n, K^{m x n}, K[x]_<=d, C over R and over C; infinite dimension.

kcs.name: Basis extension theorem
kcs.description: Independent families extend to a basis; with n = dim V, n vectors form a basis iff independent iff generating (Theorem 4.4.5).

kcs.name: Dimension of subspaces
kcs.description: dim U <= dim V with equality iff U = V, in finite dimension only (Theorem 4.4.6, Caution 4.4.7).

kcs.name: Sums and direct sums of subspaces
kcs.description: U1 + ... + Uk, direct sums, the criterion via representations of 0, U n W = {0} for two summands, and why pairwise trivial intersections are not enough (Lemma 4.5.2, Caution 4.5.3).

kcs.name: Dimension formula for sums
kcs.description: dim(U + W) + dim(U n W) = dim U + dim W (Theorem 4.5.4).

kcs.name: Complements
kcs.description: Every subspace of a finite-dimensional space has a complement of dimension dim V - dim U; complements are not unique (Corollary 4.5.6).

kcs.name: Basis of a span by row reduction
kcs.description: Write the vectors as rows, reduce, keep the non-zero rows (Task 1).

kcs.name: Basis of a solution space L(A, 0)
kcs.description: One basis vector per free variable from the reduced row echelon form (Task 2).

kcs.name: From explicit to implicit description
kcs.description: Turn a span into a system of linear equations by elimination with a symbolic right-hand side (Task 3).

kcs.name: Computing sums and intersections of subspaces
kcs.description: U + W from the union of spanning sets, U n W from the combined implicit equations (Task 4, Example 4.6.1).

kcs.name: Linear maps and examples
kcs.description: Definition 5.1.1, isomorphisms, endomorphisms, Hom and End; f_A, rotations, differentiation, evaluation, transposition; non-examples.

kcs.name: Composition, inverse and Hom(V, W)
kcs.description: Compositions and inverses of linear maps are linear; Hom(V, W) is a vector space (Lemma 5.1.3).

kcs.name: Kernel, image and rank of a linear map
kcs.description: ker f and im f are subspaces, rank f = dim im f, injective iff ker f = 0; for f_A the kernel is L(A, 0) and the image is the column span.

kcs.name: Linear maps are determined by a basis
kcs.description: A linear map is fixed by the images of a basis, which can be prescribed freely; injective iff the images are independent, isomorphism iff they form a basis (Theorem 5.1.5).

kcs.name: Coordinate isomorphism
kcs.description: Phi_B: K^n -> V; finite-dimensional spaces are isomorphic iff they have the same dimension, but not canonically (Corollary 5.1.6).

kcs.name: Rank-nullity theorem
kcs.description: dim V = dim ker f + dim im f, with its proof by basis extension (Theorem 5.2.1).

kcs.name: Injective iff surjective in equal finite dimension
kcs.description: For dim V = dim W < infinity, injective <=> surjective <=> bijective; fails in infinite dimension (Corollary 5.2.2, Caution 5.2.3).

kcs.name: Number of free variables
kcs.description: dim L(A, 0) = n - rank, so the number of free variables does not depend on the elimination (Corollary 5.2.4).

kcs.name: Matrix of a linear map
kcs.description: M^B_C(f): column j holds the C-coordinates of f(v_j); Hom(V, W) is isomorphic to K^{m x n}; M times coordinates of v gives coordinates of f(v) (Definition 5.3.1, Theorem 5.3.2).

kcs.name: Matrix product and composition
kcs.description: Definition of AB; the matrix of g o f is the product; associativity and distributivity; K^{n x n} is a non-commutative ring (Theorem 5.3.4, Corollary 5.3.5).

kcs.name: Invertible matrices
kcs.description: GL_n(K); invertible <=> f_A isomorphism <=> Ax = 0 only trivially <=> columns a basis <=> one-sided inverse (Proposition 5.3.7).

kcs.name: Computing the inverse by Gauss-Jordan
kcs.description: Row-reduce (A | I) to (I | A^-1), or find that A is not invertible (Example 5.3.8).

kcs.name: Transition matrices
kcs.description: T^{B'}_B = M^{B'}_B(id) converts B'-coordinates into B-coordinates; its inverse goes back.

kcs.name: Transformation formula and similar matrices
kcs.description: M^{B'}_{C'}(f) = T M^B_C(f) T', and S^-1 A S for endomorphisms; similar and equivalent matrices (Theorem 5.4.1, Definition 5.4.2).

kcs.name: Normal form under equivalence
kcs.description: Bases in which f has the matrix (I_r 0; 0 0); matrices are equivalent iff they have the same rank (Theorem 5.4.3).

kcs.name: Row rank equals column rank
kcs.description: rank A = rank A^T (Theorem 5.5.2).

kcs.name: Computing the rank by elimination
kcs.description: rank A is the number of non-zero rows of a row echelon form (Remark 5.5.3).

kcs.name: Solvability criterion
kcs.description: Ax = b is solvable iff rank A = rank (A | b); uniquely solvable for all b iff A is invertible (Corollary 5.5.4).

kcs.name: Quotient spaces (*)
kcs.description: V/U as cosets v + U, well-defined operations, canonical projection, dim V/U = dim V - dim U. Marked (*): not exam-relevant.

kcs.name: Homomorphism theorem (*)
kcs.description: V / ker f is isomorphic to im f via v + ker f -> f(v) (Theorem 5.6.1). Marked (*).

kcs.name: Elementary matrices
kcs.description: P_ik, D_i(lambda), T_ik(lambda) perform row operations from the left and column operations from the right; their inverses and determinants.

kcs.name: Invertible matrices as products of elementary matrices
kcs.description: EA is in reduced row echelon form for a product E of elementary matrices; A invertible iff EA = I (Theorem 5.7.1).

kcs.name: LR decomposition
kcs.description: A = LR (PA = LR with row swaps) from elimination; solving by forward and backward substitution (Remark 5.7.2).

kcs.name: Dual space and dual map
kcs.description: V* = Hom(V, K), linear forms and examples, f*: W* -> V*, phi -> phi o f.

kcs.name: Dual basis
kcs.description: v_i*(v_j) = delta_ij gives a basis of V*; v_i* reads off the i-th coordinate; V and V* are isomorphic but not canonically (Proposition 5.8.2, Caution 5.8.4).

kcs.name: Matrix of the dual map is the transpose
kcs.description: M^{C*}_{B*}(f*) = M^B_C(f)^T (Proposition 5.8.3).

kcs.name: Permutations and transpositions
kcs.description: S_n, two-row notation, transpositions; every permutation is a product of transpositions (Lemma 6.1.1).

kcs.name: Inversions and the sign
kcs.description: Counting inversions, sgn = (-1)^N, even and odd permutations, the product formula (Definition 6.1.2, Lemma 6.1.3).

kcs.name: The sign is a homomorphism
kcs.description: sgn(sigma rho) = sgn sigma sgn rho, transpositions are odd, the parity of a factorisation is fixed, A_n = ker sgn (Theorem 6.1.4).

kcs.name: Determinant functions and their rules
kcs.description: Multilinear, alternating, normalised; swapping columns changes the sign, adding a multiple of a column changes nothing, dependent columns give 0 (Definition 6.2.1, Lemma 6.2.2).

kcs.name: Leibniz formula, 2x2, Sarrus and triangular matrices
kcs.description: Existence and uniqueness of det, the Leibniz formula, ad - bc, the rule of Sarrus, det of a triangular matrix (Theorem 6.2.3, Examples 6.2.4).

kcs.name: Multiplicativity of the determinant
kcs.description: det(AB) = det A det B (Theorem 6.3.1(a)).

kcs.name: Invertible iff det is non-zero
kcs.description: A invertible <=> det A != 0, and det(A^-1) = (det A)^-1 (Theorem 6.3.1(b)).

kcs.name: Determinant of the transpose
kcs.description: det A^T = det A, so every column rule holds for rows (Theorem 6.3.1(c)).

kcs.name: Determinant of an endomorphism and scaling
kcs.description: Similar matrices have the same determinant, so det f is defined; det(lambda A) = lambda^n det A, det is not additive (Theorem 6.3.1(d), Remark 6.3.2).

kcs.name: Computing determinants by row reduction
kcs.description: Reduce to triangular form, tracking sign changes and factors (Example 6.3.3).

kcs.name: Block triangular matrices
kcs.description: det (A B; 0 C) = det A det C (Proposition 6.3.4).

kcs.name: Laplace expansion
kcs.description: Expansion along any row or column with signs (-1)^(i+j) and minors (Theorem 6.4.1).

kcs.name: Vandermonde determinant and interpolation
kcs.description: V(x1, ..., xn) = product of (xj - xi); unique interpolation polynomial for distinct nodes (Example 6.4.2).

kcs.name: Adjugate and the inverse formula
kcs.description: A adj(A) = det(A) I, so A^-1 = adj(A)/det A (Theorem 6.4.4).

kcs.name: Cramer's rule
kcs.description: x_j = det(A with column j replaced by b) / det A (Corollary 6.4.5).

kcs.name: Geometric meaning of the determinant
kcs.description: |det A| scales areas and volumes, its sign records orientation (chapter intro, Remark 6.4.6).
assumes: Area, volume and orientation in plane geometry

kcs.name: Eigenvalues, eigenvectors and eigenspaces
kcs.description: f(v) = lambda v with v != 0, Eig(f, lambda) = ker(f - lambda id); reflection, rotation, the Jordan block J, differentiation (Definition 7.1.1, Examples 7.1.3).

kcs.name: Diagonalisability
kcs.description: A basis of eigenvectors; A is diagonalisable iff S^-1 A S is diagonal, with eigenvectors as the columns of S (Lemma 7.1.2).

kcs.name: Eigenvectors for distinct eigenvalues are independent
kcs.description: The sum of eigenspaces is direct; at most n eigenvalues; n distinct eigenvalues imply diagonalisable (Theorem 7.1.4, Corollary 7.1.5).

kcs.name: Characteristic polynomial
kcs.description: chi_A = det(xI - A); the eigenvalues are its roots in K; chi for 2x2 matrices (Definition 7.2.1, Proposition 7.2.2(c), Example 7.2.3).

kcs.name: Trace and determinant in the characteristic polynomial
kcs.description: chi_A = x^n - tr(A) x^(n-1) + ... + (-1)^n det A; chi, tr and det are similarity invariants (Proposition 7.2.2(a, b)).

kcs.name: Algebraic and geometric multiplicity
kcs.description: mu_a as root multiplicity, mu_g = dim Eig; 1 <= mu_g <= mu_a (Definition 7.2.4, Lemma 7.2.5).

kcs.name: Diagonalisability criterion
kcs.description: Diagonalisable <=> V is the direct sum of the eigenspaces <=> chi splits and mu_g = mu_a for every eigenvalue (Theorem 7.3.1, Example 7.3.3).

kcs.name: Diagonalising a matrix
kcs.description: Compute chi and its roots, a basis of each eigenspace by elimination, and S with S^-1 A S diagonal (Algorithm, Example 7.3.2).

kcs.name: Matrix powers and linear recursions
kcs.description: A^k = S D^k S^-1; Fibonacci numbers and Binet's formula (Section 7.4).

kcs.name: Real and complex eigenvalues
kcs.description: A rotation has no real eigenvalue but e^(+-i phi) over C; every complex matrix has an eigenvalue (Example 7.2.3).

kcs.name: Invariant subspaces
kcs.description: f-invariant subspaces give a block triangular matrix, chi of the restriction divides chi_f, and invariant complements give block diagonal form (Supplement).

kcs.name: Projections
kcs.description: f o f = f implies V = ker f (+) im f, f is diagonalisable with eigenvalues in {0, 1}, and tr f = rank f (Final exam Problem 5).

kcs.name: Nilpotent matrices
kcs.description: A^k = 0: only eigenvalue 0, I - A invertible with the geometric series, diagonalisable only if A = 0, and A^n = 0 (Resit Problem 6).

kcs.name: Kernel chains of powers
kcs.description: ker f subset ker f^2 subset ..., which becomes stationary at the latest at n (Exercise 18).

kcs.name: Rank of sums and products
kcs.description: rank(A + B) <= rank A + rank B and rank(AB) <= min(rank A, rank B) (Exercise 16, Final exam Problem 6(b)).

kcs.name: Cayley-Hamilton for 2x2 matrices
kcs.description: A^2 - tr(A) A + det(A) I = 0, and the inverse formula from it (Exercise 24, Final exam Problem 1(d)).

kcs.name: Symmetric and skew-symmetric matrices
kcs.description: K^{n x n} = Sym_n (+) Skew_n when char K != 2, with dimensions n(n+1)/2 and n(n-1)/2 (Exercise 12).
